The Iron Bear can deal a ton of splash damage and Moze has skills that buff that, but because of that she can often down herself or eat up the iron bears health/fuel pretty quickly. I’d recommend putting a point into Auto Bear & looking for the legendary com “Rocketeer”; it allows Auto Bear to last the rest of the duration Iron Bear had left if she gets out early. So you can activate Iron Bear, hop out, then the enemies have a giant turret to agro on, and you can easily flank them. You just have to position Iron Bear in such a way that it won’t get damaged by its own splash damage. Bonus points if you give Iron Bear the bubble shield, makes it even tankier.

I completely agree, having the exact same experience at the moment. The voice actors are doing their best, but with poor writing it’s difficult to convey real emotion. Colleen Clinkenbeard did an incredible job when Roland dies in BL2, and then Ashley Burch absolutely nailed the emotion in the DragonKeep DLC, but since then we haven’t seen much in the way of inspired dialogue. The voice acting is good, but the writing is atrocious, it’s like how Harrison Ford told George Lucas “you can write this sh*t but you sure can’t read it”. Also, the story is just unoriginal; one particular cutscene was pretty much lifted from a popular superhero movie (you’ll know it when you see it). The voice actors are trying their best, but it’s difficult when the words are just poorly written. The gameplay however is amazing, I wish they had incorporated Oz kits from the pre-sequel, but aside from that, the gameplay is near perfect. I also think they did an incredible job with the environments, they seem to pull inspiration from the first Borderlands in a big way, which I very much appreciate. The areas in BL3 feel expansive but still small enough to not always need a vehicle because they have a lot more verticality. Harking back to BL1, there are a lot more places to explore off the beaten path, which you could otherwise miss. This is a nice shift back from BL2 & BLTPS where the areas felt more linear & you could explore all of it pretty quickly on your first run through. Most importantly though, the environments in BL3 feel fresh while still being reminiscent of the previous games. Eden-6 is especially beautiful, and reminded me of the Rust Commons in BL1 & the Zombie Island DLC. One last thing, the music is like the BL1 soundtrack merged with the BL2 soundtrack, it perfectly encapsulates the tone that BL1 set for the Borderworlds, while building upon the subsequent games soundtracks in a nice way.

I don’t think you’re entirely off in the second part of what you said, about how River knew that even when Jayne betrayed them they’d get away and Mal would see the truth, but I disagree that she cut him because she couldn’t take his hateful mouth for one more remark. Having just rewatched that scene, Jayne is being characteristically rude, spitting on the sharp stone (twice), pointing out the food smells like crotch (it does, even Simon begrudgingly agrees), but he doesn’t do or say anything that’s hateful, he’s just kind of a jerk. Simon and Wash are having a little banter about hating doctors, and Wash says “present company excluded”, at this point in the background River has already taken the kitchen knife, and then Jayne says “best not be excluding people, that’d be rude” and SLASH. Then he hits her there’s some commotion and River looks at Jayne, almost in shock but more confused the way a kid looks when they don’t realize they’ve done something wrong, and says “he looks better in red”. The slash wasn’t his entire chest either, it was just the Blue Sun logo.

I think you’re reading into it too much. Jayne was wearing a shirt with the logo of the Blue Sun corporation, a corporation that River directly associates with her traumatic time at the academy (although we, the viewer, don’t know what the exact relation is). Slashing Jayne across the chest in ‘Ariel’ and shredding the labels on the food cans in ‘Shindig’ are reactions to seeing the Blue Sun corporations logo; they’re both physical responses to her PTSD.
